messages:
olivia: Heads-up — customer question from Acme: they want a clear list of which audit fields are included in customer-facing delivery (webhooks + S3 export) and how RBAC changes affect visibility. Also worried about KMS key rotation breaking archived S3 exports. Any concise summary we can send? :shield:

ryan: Short answer: webhook + S3 exports include the event envelope + payload we defined in schema v2. RBAC affects only the control-plane visibility (who can configure exports / view raw events in Console). The events themselves contain actor/principal fields as recorded, not filtered by downstream RBAC. :eyes:

olivia: Do we have a one-liner for customers about "what you will see" vs "what console admins can view"? They need that for their compliance team.

ryan: Proposed two-line: "Audit exports (webhook/S3) contain event metadata and payload per schema v2 (event_type, timestamp, actor_id, actor_role, resource, outcome, request_context). Console RBAC controls who can configure and access exports; it does not rewrite audit event actor fields."

devops-bot: Deploy completed: audit-schema:v2 -> production (2024-11-07T14:12Z).

kevin: KMS rotation: S3 exports are server-side encrypted with customer-managed KMS (if they opted in). Rotation doesn't invalidate already-written objects as long as the KMS key exists and new key version is authorized to decrypt. If key is deleted or policy changes to block decrypt, archived files become unreadable. Recommend we note: "retain key or export prior to deletion".

sarah: Also note PII policy: we mask IP addresses in exported events when customer picks "mask_ip": true flag. Default is false. Some customers require masked IPs by default — ops will change config per contract.

olivia: Can we show an example event snippet for their security team? Keep it redacted (no real PII).

ryan: Example (truncated):
```json
{
  "schema_version": "v2",
  "event_id": "evt_01F...",
  "timestamp": "2025-02-18T21:03:15Z",
  "event_type": "model.inference.invoke",
  "actor": {
    "actor_id": "user_123",
    "actor_role": "product-engineer",
    "ip_address": "REDACTED"
  },
  "resource": {
    "resource_type": "deployment",
    "resource_id": "dep_456"
  },
  "request_context": {
    "client": "api-key",
    "user_agent": "Acme/1.2"
  },
  "outcome": "success",
  "details": { "tokens": 42 }
}
```

kevin: For webhooks we publish the following headers for verification: `X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=<hex>` and `X-Redwood-Schema: v2`. Example verification command customers can use:
```
echo -n '$BODY' | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac '$WEBHOOK_SECRET'
```
Then compare hex to the signature header. We should include this snippet in onboarding docs.

olivia: Good. Any SIEM mapping notes? Splunk/Datadog teams asked about field names.

ryan: Mapping notes: suggest mapping `event_type` -> `event_type`, `timestamp` -> `_time`, `actor.actor_id` -> `user`, `actor.actor_role` -> `user_role`, `resource.resource_id` -> `object_id`, `outcome` -> `result`. For Splunk, include `sourcetype=redwood:audit:v2`. For Datadog logs use `service:redwood-audit` and `ddsource:api`.

sarah: Also call out sampling / redaction: we will never include prompt text in exports by default. There is an opt-in for full request logs for enterprise customers — that is gated by contract and extra retention/PII controls.

kevin: On onboarding checklist: 1) provide webhook URL + secret or S3 bucket ARN + KMS key id 2) confirm mask_ip flag 3) choose schema version (we default v2) 4) provide SIEM field mapping preferences if needed 5) run validation script we provide.

olivia: Do we have the validation script URL?

devops-bot: File uploaded: https://redwood.internal/artifacts/audit-validation-script-2025-02-18.sh

ryan: Quick validation example (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://hooks.acme.com/redwood -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=<sig>' -d '{"schema_version":"v2","event_type":"test.ping"}'
```
We include a sample response with 200 + `x-redwood-validated: true` header when signature checks out.

sarah: Action items: I'll update the customer-facing FAQ to include the short one-liner, the sample event, and PII redaction policy. Kevin — can you add the webhook signature snippet to onboarding template?

kevin: Yep, will do today.

olivia: Thanks team — I'll reply to Acme with the one-liner + link to validation script and ask if they want masked IPs by default. :thumbsup:
